newsitem.title: UK: HOUSING SHORTAGE SQUEEZES PRICES THROUGH ROOF.
newsitem.headline: HOUSING SHORTAGE SQUEEZES PRICES THROUGH ROOF.

text.p: A shortage of available properties are squeezing British house prices through the roof, a report said on Tuesday.

The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors said the dearth of properties for sale was so bad that homeowners were delaying putting their homes on the market until they had found a new one to buy. That has simply made the situation worse -- "a self-perpetuating cycle of frustration," the RICS called it.
It said many potential housebuyers may also be holding off until this summer's avalanche of windfall payments from building societies has been reaped.

A number of major building societies are converting into banks, quoted on the stock exchange, later this year. A total of about 17 billion sterling ($28 billion) will flood into consumers' pockets as a result of this process.
"Hopes of even higher prices have led to unrealistic expectations and disillusionment among prospective sellers," said RICS housing market spokesman Ian Perry.
Worst hit by the lack of homes for sale was London and the South East, where prices jumped accordingly, the RICS said. Most in demand were larger family homes and country properties.
Perry added that house prices were likely to continue climbing in the short term, given that interest rates were unlikely to rise before elections which must be held by May.
But later in the year, as rates rise and more property comes onto the market, the steam should be taken out of house price inflation, Perry said.
The RICS survey showed a net balance of 48 percent of chartered surveyors reported higher prices in January.
The Institute's quarterly survey of the housing market quizzed 268 chartered surveyors over changes in prices and the level of homes sold or for sale. ($ = 0.617 British Pounds Sterling)
